comment:
Single source of truth for connectors.lock.yaml, the per install record of what a bundle's declared connector source resolved to (ADR 0113). Python owns ConnectorLockFile / ConnectorLockEntry, validate_connector_lock and apply_lock in packages/plugin-format/src/plugin_format/connector_lock.py; the Rust CLI owns hand mirrors in cli/src/connector_build.rs because `curie build` writes the file and `curie cluster deploy` preflights it, both before the platform ever sees the bundle. plugin-format.schema.json carries no Connector* $defs, so the schema driven field-parity gate compares nothing here and this file is the seam instead. Read by packages/plugin-format/tests/test_connector_lock.py and by cli/tests/connector_build_decl_vectors.rs.

apply_lock is the SINGLE enforcement point for "the resolved digest is the only identity rendered into a Deployment or used to start the local connector" (ADR 0113). It returns a derived ConnectorsFile in which each build: connector's image is the locked digest and its build is cleared, so every downstream reader (render, mcp_entry, is_hosted, the worker reconciler's plan) works unchanged against an ordinary image: spec.

An image reference is well formed in exactly two shapes and nothing else: `<repo>@sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` for delivery `registry`, which is the OCI content-addressable manifest digest form documented at https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#pulling-manifests, and a bare `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` for delivery `local-daemon`, which is the image ID `docker image inspect --format {{.Id}}` reports for a locally built image. Anything else, a tag included, is refused: a tag can be repointed after review, which is the mutable-tag failure this platform has already hit.

Each vector carries: `name`, `why`, `connectors` (the connectors.yaml content), `lock` (the connectors.lock.yaml content), `portable` (the apply_lock keyword; only the cluster deploy preflight passes true), `expect` ("apply", "raise" or "invalid"), and on "apply" a `resolved` map of connector name to the image every downstream reader must then see. "raise" means validate_connector_lock accepts the document but apply_lock refuses it. "invalid" means the document does not survive validate_connector_lock at all, so it is rejected at bundle intake rather than at render time; `codes` names the reported error codes, all of which are namespaced under `connectors.lock`. Both lanes reject unknown keys inside a vector.

ADR 0173 adds an optional top-level `runner:` to both files. connector_lock.resolve_runner_image(connectors, lock, portable=...) is the single resolver for it: a vector may carry `resolved_runner` (the image it must return, or null when no runner is declared). On "raise" the Python lane runs apply_lock then resolve_runner_image and requires a ValueError from that sequence. The runner entry's `image` AND `base` must both be digest shaped for its delivery; the Rust reader refuses a tag in either at the read (SHAPE_REFUSALS in cli/tests/connector_build_decl_vectors.rs).

vectors.name: a_registry_entry_resolves_the_declaration_to_its_digest
vectors.why: The ordinary cluster path. After apply_lock the spec is indistinguishable from a hand authored image: connector, which is what lets render, mcp_entry and the reconciler stay unchanged.

vectors.name: a_local_daemon_entry_applies_when_portability_is_not_required
vectors.why: The dev fast path. A local tier version is a legitimate stored artifact and rendering its manifests is harmless because nothing applies them at local tier, so the API render path passes portable=false. Refusing here is what broke every `curie local deploy` in an earlier draft.

vectors.name: a_local_daemon_entry_is_refused_where_portability_is_required
vectors.why: A local image id names nothing a Kubernetes node can pull. Applying it produces an ImagePullBackOff on every node, long after the deploy reported success. The refusal belongs to the cluster path only, which is the sole caller passing portable=true.

vectors.name: a_tag_shaped_image_is_refused
vectors.why: The mutable-tag failure mode ADR 0113 exists to close: a tag can be repointed at a different artifact after review and between tier runs. This is the outcome test for "the renderer and applier never deploy a mutable connector tag", and it must refuse even though the reference is otherwise perfectly well formed.

vectors.name: a_truncated_digest_is_refused
vectors.why: A digest that is the right shape but the wrong length resolves to nothing. Accepting it means the refusal is a substring check for `@sha256:` rather than a check of the digest itself, which a hand edited lock trips immediately.

vectors.name: an_uppercase_digest_is_refused
vectors.why: An OCI digest is lowercase hex by specification, and two spellings of one digest would compare unequal everywhere the lock is checked for staleness or matched against a registry manifest.

vectors.name: a_bare_digest_is_refused_for_registry_delivery
vectors.why: A local image id carries no repository, so nothing can pull it. Delivery and image shape must agree or the two fields are decoration.

vectors.name: a_declared_build_connector_with_no_lock_entry_is_refused
vectors.why: Without this the derived spec keeps image None and render_deployment emits `image: null`, which applies as an invalid Deployment and surfaces as an opaque Kubernetes error far from the cause.

vectors.name: an_image_connector_is_carried_through_untouched
vectors.why: REGRESSION. apply_lock runs on every version the API renders, including the bundles in the wild that declare no build at all. A lock entry is not required for them and their image must survive byte identical.

vectors.name: a_url_connector_survives_a_lock_that_does_not_mention_it
vectors.why: REGRESSION for the remote form. A bundle mixing a built connector and a provider owned endpoint must keep the endpoint exactly as declared; only the built one is rewritten.

vectors.name: an_unknown_key_in_a_lock_entry_is_rejected_at_intake
vectors.why: The deny_unknown_fields proof for the lock. `digest:` is a plausible thing to reach for beside `image:`; silently dropping it means an operator believes they pinned something they did not. Rejected by validate_connector_lock, so a malformed lock never reaches apply_lock.

vectors.name: an_unknown_delivery_is_rejected_at_intake
vectors.why: Delivery is control bearing: it decides whether the cluster preflight refuses. An unmodelled value must be refused loudly rather than degraded to a default, the same rule ADR 0036 sets for control bearing enums.

vectors.name: an_unknown_lock_version_is_rejected_at_intake
vectors.why: The version field is the only thing that lets a future shape change be refused by an older reader instead of silently misread. A reader that ignores it makes the field decoration.

vectors.name: a_registry_runner_entry_resolves_to_its_digest
vectors.why: ADR 0173 decision 2: the renderer uses exactly the recorded runner digest and nothing derived from a tag.

vectors.name: a_bundle_declaring_no_runner_resolves_no_runner_image
vectors.why: REGRESSION. Every bundle in the wild declares no runner and must keep the platform runner, so the resolver answers None rather than raising for a lock without a runner entry.

vectors.name: a_local_daemon_runner_entry_applies_when_portability_is_not_required
vectors.why: The dev fast path, same as for connectors: a local image id is a legitimate identity where nothing pulls it.

vectors.name: a_local_daemon_runner_entry_is_refused_where_portability_is_required
vectors.why: No cluster node can pull an image that lives only in the operator's Docker daemon; sandboxes would sit in ImagePullBackOff.

vectors.name: a_tag_shaped_runner_image_is_refused
vectors.why: The mutable-tag failure ADR 0173 inherits from ADR 0113: a tag can be repointed after review.

vectors.name: a_tag_shaped_runner_base_is_refused
vectors.why: The base is recorded so an upgrade can tell which platform runner a layer was built on. A tag there answers that question with whatever the tag points at today.

vectors.name: a_declared_runner_with_no_lock_entry_is_refused
vectors.why: Falling back to the platform runner would silently drop every tool the bundle's layer installs; the agent then fails mid-turn on a missing binary.

vectors.name: an_unknown_key_in_the_runner_entry_is_rejected_at_intake
vectors.why: The deny_unknown_fields proof for RunnerLockEntry.
